title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every dimension
subject: Topology
plain_english: Any locally compact group acting faithfully and continuously on a finite-dimensional manifold is a Lie group; in particular the p-adic integers cannot act this way.
opportunity: None. This is transformation-group theory. The continuous symmetry groups used in physics, robotics or vision are Lie groups by construction, so nothing downstream changes.
caveats: Long-open major conjecture with no formalization; treat as unverified claim.

title: Four-dimensional disk embedding and Wall's conjecture
subject: Topology
plain_english: In 4-dimensional topology the Freedman-Quinn disk-embedding tool fails without fundamental-group hypotheses (the free group F2 is not 'good'), and there is a 4-dimensional Poincare duality group that is not the fundamental group of any closed aspherical 4-manifold.
constructive: yes - explicit 4-manifolds/disc maps and a finitely presented group, but purely topological objects
opportunity: None. Topological 4-manifold surgery theory has no computational or engineering consumer.
caveats: Three unformalized manuscripts; resolves a central open question (F2 goodness), so high scrutiny is warranted.

title: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture
subject: Topology
plain_english: Two different Dehn surgeries on a nontrivial knot in the 3-sphere never give the same oriented 3-manifold.
opportunity: None. Software that enumerates or identifies 3-manifolds (SnapPy, Regina) identifies surgeries computationally already; the theorem removes no computational step and gives no new invariant to implement.

title: Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
subject: Topology
plain_english: Builds an explicit family of bounded-degree finite graphs (finite quotients of SL3(Z) placed over discs in the triangular lattice) on which the coarse assembly map from index theory kills a nonzero K-homology class, disproving the coarse Novikov conjecture (reduced and maximal versions).
constructive: yes - explicit graph family, but the phenomenon is asymptotic in disc radius and lives in operator K-theory/Roe algebras
explicit_constants: graph family explicit; no quantitative sizes relevant to practice
opportunity: None. Coarse assembly/Roe algebras are unrelated to topological data analysis (persistent homology does not compute coarse K-homology), and the graphs are just congruence Cayley graphs with property (T) -- no new expander construction or benchmark use beyond what Margulis/LPS graphs already give.
caveats: Reduced-assembly counterexample is Lean-formalized (CoarseAssembly); maximal version is not.

title: Finite Smith–Toda complexes at every height
subject: Topology
plain_english: Constructs finite spectra V(n) (generalized Moore spectra) with prescribed Brown-Peterson homology at every height, at a prime depending on n (e.g. V(4) at p=1009).
constructive: yes - explicit finite spectra, but objects of stable homotopy theory
opportunity: None. Chromatic stable homotopy theory has no applied consumer.

title: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three
subject: Topology
plain_english: At the prime 3, the Kervaire invariant classes survive in the Adams spectral sequence exactly in stems 10, 106, 322.
constructive: partial - detection via equivariant Morava E-theory; no algorithmic output
opportunity: None. Computational stable-homotopy software (Bruner's ext, Lin/Wang/Xu machine computations) works at p=2 in low stems; stem 106/322 at p=3 is far outside any computed range and the result changes no code.
caveats: Long-open problem, unformalized; relies on Belmont-Ray coefficient model proved here.

title: Quillen's conjecture in rational homology
subject: Topology
plain_english: If a finite group has no nontrivial normal p-subgroup, then the poset of its nontrivial elementary abelian p-subgroups has nonzero rational homology (Quillen's conjecture).
opportunity: None. Could be spot-checked in GAP/Magma for small groups, but no algorithm or application uses subgroup-poset contractibility.

title: The Hovey–Strickland and Chai conjectures
subject: Topology
plain_english: Classifies invariant prime ideals of Lubin-Tate rings (Chai's conjecture) and hence the thick tensor ideals of dualizable K(n)-local spectra (Hovey-Strickland).
opportunity: None (chromatic homotopy theory).

title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis
subject: Topology
plain_english: Grothendieck's algebraic definition of infinity-groupoids (freely add all coherence operations via a 'coherator') reproduces exactly the homotopy theory of topological spaces, for every coherator in the Ara-Henry convention; the key step is Henry's pushout conjecture.
constructive: partial - explicit path/cylinder constructions interpreting every coherator operation, but the output is an equivalence of homotopy theories, not an algorithm
opportunity: No effect on mainstream HoTT/proof-assistant practice: Coq-HoTT, Cubical Agda and Lean already rest on simplicial/cubical/infinity-topos semantics (Kapulkin-Lumsdaine, Shulman) that interpret types as spaces. The one real formal-methods touchpoint is coherator-based type theories such as CaTT (Finster-Mimram), whose models are Grothendieck-Maltsiniotis weak omega-categories (Benjamin-Finster-Mimram): if a groupoidal CaTT/Brunerie-style coherator fits the Ara-Henry height convention, this theorem gives it a 'models = spaces' semantics. The Lean development of the elementary-expansion theorem (~12.7k lines, OAI/CategoryTheory/Globular) is a possible Mathlib contribution on globular theories.
targets: CaTT (Finster-Mimram type theory / proof assistant for weak omega-categories)
first_step: Check whether Brunerie's groupoidal coherator / the CaTT groupoid fragment satisfies Definition 'coherator convention' (generating fillers of output dimension j have arity height <= j); if so, send the semantic corollary to the CaTT developers.
caveats: Lean covers only the elementary-expansion (Henry pushout) theorem, not the semi-model structure or comparison with spaces; benefit is to type-theory semantics, not industrial verification.

title: Finite generation for the $`K(n)`$-local sphere
subject: Topology
plain_english: Every homotopy group of the K(n)-local sphere is a finitely generated p-adic module.
opportunity: None (chromatic homotopy theory).

title: Cyclic length and chromatic fixed-point loss
subject: Topology
plain_english: For a subgroup H of a finite p-group G, the chromatic height lost passing from H- to G-geometric fixed points equals the shortest subnormal chain from H to G with cyclic quotients.
constructive: partial - sharpness witnessed by finite spectra
opportunity: None (equivariant chromatic homotopy theory).

title: The four-dimensional Singer conjecture
subject: Topology
plain_english: For closed aspherical 4-manifolds (and 4-dimensional Poincare complexes), L2-Betti numbers of the universal cover vanish outside the middle degree (Singer conjecture in dimension 4).
opportunity: None. L2-invariants have no applied consumer here.

title: Curtis’s conjecture
subject: Topology
plain_english: The mod-2 stable Hurewicz image of the sphere is spanned by the Hopf-invariant-one and Kervaire-invariant-one classes (Curtis's conjecture).
opportunity: None (stable homotopy theory).
caveats: Unformalized; earlier proposed proof had a gap (Wellington), per the introduction.

title: Thomason model structures in all strict higher dimensions
subject: Topology
plain_english: Strict n-categories (every finite n and n = omega) carry a Thomason-type model structure Quillen-equivalent to simplicial sets, so strict higher categories model all homotopy types.
constructive: yes - explicit Quillen adjunction c_n Sd^2 -| Ex^2 N_n (Street nerve), fully Lean-formalized
opportunity: Not a HoTT result (it concerns strict, not weak, categories) and changes no proof assistant's semantics. The concrete asset is the ~160k-line Lean 4 development (OAI/CategoryTheory/Thomason) built on Mathlib's SSet.modelCategoryQuillen: strict omega-categories, Street nerve, Sd/Ex, Gray-type prisms, model-structure transfer. Upstreaming reusable layers would fill gaps in Mathlib's higher-category/homotopical-algebra library and could serve the Lean infinity-cosmos effort and polygraph/higher-rewriting formalizations.
first_step: Extract the OmegaCategory/Street-nerve/Ex^2-Sd^2 layers into a standalone branch against current Mathlib and open a Zulip discussion with the homotopical-algebra maintainers about upstreaming.
caveats: Value is to formal-mathematics infrastructure only; upstreaming 160k machine-written lines is a multi-month refactoring job.

title: Chromatic splitting: filtrations and counterexamples
subject: Topology
plain_english: Disproves strong and weak chromatic splitting in several height/prime ranges, while showing the relevant chromatic overlap still admits a 2^n-stage filtration by the predicted pieces.
constructive: partial - explicit filtrations and kernel classes
opportunity: None (chromatic homotopy theory).

title: Counterexamples to finite generation at chromatic height two
subject: Topology
plain_english: For large primes, constructs a spectrum of fp-type two that cannot be built from completed BP<2> by finitely many cofibers, refuting the Hahn-Wilson conjecture at height two.
opportunity: None (chromatic homotopy theory).

title: Nonhomeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds
subject: Topology
plain_english: There are closed aspherical 4-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic (counterexample to the Borel conjecture in dimension 4).
constructive: yes - explicit manifolds with hyperbolic fundamental group
opportunity: None.
caveats: Counterexample to a famous conjecture, unformalized.

title: A counterexample to Wall's finite D(2) problem
subject: Topology
plain_english: A finite 3-dimensional CW complex that satisfies Wall's D(2) homological condition but has no 2-dimensional finite model (built via Quillen's plus construction; obstruction from rank-one local systems).
constructive: yes - explicit complex via plus construction
opportunity: None. Related to group presentations/relation gaps (and distantly to Andrews-Curtis), but gives no algorithm or benchmark of practical interest.

title: Smooth isometric immersions of surfaces into ℝ<sup>4</sup>
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: Every closed smooth Riemannian surface (any curvature, orientable or not) can be realized exactly as a smooth, possibly self-intersecting, surface in 4-dimensional Euclidean space.
constructive: partial - Nash-type iteration with smoothing and an infinite correction scheme; existence, not an implementable algorithm
opportunity: None. Graphics, shape analysis and manifold learning only need C^1 or approximate isometric embeddings (Nash-Kuiper corrugations already give C^1 isometric embeddings of surfaces in R^3; Verma-style manifold-learning embeddings aim at approximate isometry), and nobody processes exact smooth isometric immersions in R^4.

title: A smooth surface metric with no local isometric immersion in ℝ<sup>3</sup>
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: There is a smooth surface metric, flat to infinite order at a point, that cannot be realized as a smooth surface in 3-space on any neighbourhood of that point.
explicit_constants: explicit construction, but not useful as test data
opportunity: None. The obvious applied consumer would be inverse design of shape-morphing sheets (non-Euclidean plates, nematic-elastomer and growth-programmed surfaces), but designed metrics are analytic or have nondegenerate curvature, where local immersions exist (Janet-Cartan, Lin). The counterexample needs curvature sign changes accumulating at an infinitely degenerate point -- physically irrelevant.

title: Gromov’s integral scalar-curvature bound for simplicial volume
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: Negative scalar curvature, integrated suitably, bounds the simplicial volume of a manifold; also manifolds with positive scalar curvature are rationally inessential (Gromov-Lawson aspherical conjecture).
opportunity: None. Positive-mass-type consequences in general relativity are already known by other methods.

title: Spectral scalar curvature, Urysohn width, and macroscopic dimension
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: Manifolds with (spectral) positive scalar curvature are macroscopically at most (n-2)-dimensional: they map to an (n-2)-complex with uniformly small fibres.
constructive: partial - existence of maps; explicit fibre bound 500/sqrt(lambda) in dimension 3
explicit_constants: 3D: fibre diameter <= 500/sqrt(lambda); higher n: dimension-only constant
opportunity: None.

title: Sharp Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry and rigidity
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: In simply connected spaces of nonpositive curvature, no region of a given volume has smaller boundary than the model ball; and any cycle in a CAT(0) space bounds a filling no larger than in Euclidean space, with the sharp constant.
constructive: partial - filling existence with sharp Euclidean constant
opportunity: None found. CAT(0) spaces do appear in practice -- BHV phylogenetic tree space (statistics on trees), CAT(0) cube complexes of reconfigurable-robot state spaces (Ghrist; Ardila et al. motion planning), hyperbolic embeddings in ML -- but those algorithms use geodesics and Frechet means, never filling/isoperimetric bounds.
caveats: CAT(0) filling version Lean-formalized; manifold Cartan-Hadamard version is not.

title: Yau's uniformization conjecture
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: A complete noncompact Kahler manifold with positive bisectional curvature is biholomorphic to C^n (Yau's uniformization conjecture).
opportunity: None.

title: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: For negatively curved closed manifolds of dimension >= 3, the Liouville measure is the measure of maximal entropy for the geodesic flow only if the metric is locally symmetric (Katok's conjecture).
opportunity: None.

title: A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: In a cotangent bundle of S^9 x S^(N-1) for some large even N there is an exact Lagrangian diffeomorphic to the zero section but not Hamiltonian isotopic to it (nearby Lagrangian conjecture fails).
constructive: partial - existence for unspecified large N
opportunity: None.

title: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: Any normalized hypersymplectic triple of 2-forms on a closed 4-manifold can be deformed to a hyperkahler triple in the same cohomology classes (Donaldson).
opportunity: None.
caveats: Manuscript was revised on Oct 7 2026 (dependency removed); unformalized.

title: Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: On a closed 4-manifold, an almost complex structure tamed by some symplectic form is compatible with some symplectic form (Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture).
opportunity: None.
caveats: Lean-formalized main statement; the paper's cone-equality claim was corrected on Oct 7 2026.

title: Symplectic ball packing in higher dimensions
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: In dimension 6 and up, finitely many symplectic balls fit disjointly into a symplectic ball exactly when total volume fits and every pair of radii (capacities) sums to less than the big one.
constructive: partial - embeddings produced by deformation/Moser arguments over toric models; no explicit symplectomorphisms
opportunity: None. Applied phase-space uses of symplectic rigidity (beam emittance and the 'symplectic camel', de Gosson's quantum blobs, symplectic integrators) rely on single-ball non-squeezing, not multi-ball packing in dimension >= 6, and the theorem says the only obstructions there are volume plus Gromov's two-ball bound -- i.e., less rigidity, nothing to design against.

title: The metric Blaschke conjecture
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: A closed manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is a round sphere or projective space up to scale (metric Blaschke conjecture).
opportunity: None.

title: Infinitely many closed geodesics on Riemannian spheres and closed three-manifolds
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: Every Riemannian metric on a sphere (and on every closed 3-manifold) has infinitely many geometrically distinct closed geodesics.
opportunity: None. Geodesic computation on meshes (heat method, MMP) does not depend on counts of closed geodesics.

title: Sharp singular-set bounds for stationary integral varifolds
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: For every stationary (minimal-surface-like) integral varifold, the singular set has dimension at most m-1, and is measure-zero; sharp in all dimensions/codimensions.
opportunity: None. Physical soap films already obey Taylor's classification of singularities, and computational tools (Surface Evolver; varifold shape metrics of Charon-Trouve used in Deformetrica) use varifolds as measures or meshes, independent of this regularity.
caveats: Unformalized; resolves a recent Brena-Decio-De Lellis conjecture with a sharp bound.

title: Counterexamples to stable-Morse and strong Arnold fixed-point bounds
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms can have fewer fixed points than Morse theory of the underlying manifold suggests (counterexamples in dimensions 6, 12, 22, 3332).
constructive: yes - explicit Kahler manifolds/Hamiltonians, but very high dimensional
opportunity: None. Counts of periodic orbits in applied Hamiltonian dynamics (celestial mechanics, plasma) live on low-dimensional, non-compact or specific phase spaces; these Kahler examples change no lower bound anyone uses.
caveats: Only the quadric-threefold (degenerate) example is Lean-formalized.

title: Nonnegative-curvature Einstein classification and an L2 topological gap
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: Classifies positive Einstein 4-manifolds with nonnegative sectional curvature (S^4, CP^2, S^2xS^2) and gives an L^2 trace-free-Ricci gap theorem.
opportunity: None.
caveats: Strictly-positive-curvature classification Lean-formalized; zero-plane and L^2 gap parts not.

title: The Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: Every non-totally-geodesic closed minimal hypersurface in a round sphere has at least the area of the smallest Clifford minimal hypersurface (Solomon-Yau).
opportunity: None.

title: Yau’s nodal bounds: surfaces and higher dimensions
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: On any fixed smooth closed surface, the zero set of a Laplace eigenfunction with eigenvalue lambda has length at most C*sqrt(lambda); in dimensions 3-5 the analogous bound fails for some smooth (non-analytic) metrics.
constructive: no - existence of a metric-dependent constant obtained through compactness/contradiction arguments; counterexamples are explicit but non-analytic
opportunity: None in practice. Users of eigenfunction nodal sets (spectral mesh segmentation and manifold harmonics in geometry processing, Laplacian positional encodings in geometric deep learning, Chladni/vibration analysis, quantum-chaos random-wave statistics) work with PL meshes or analytic metrics, where sqrt(k) scaling was already known (Donnelly-Fefferman) or observed; the constant is non-explicit, and the 3D-5D counterexamples require infinitely fine smooth metric tuning that no physical or discretized metric has.

title: Scalar curvature and finite-time Ricci-flow singularities
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: 4-dimensional Ricci flow continues as long as scalar curvature stays bounded; in high dimensions this fails.
opportunity: None. Applied 'Ricci flow' is either discrete 2D surface Ricci flow for conformal parametrization (Gu-Yau; fully understood) or Ollivier/Forman graph curvature flows for networks/GNN rewiring -- neither is 4D smooth flow.

title: A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: Calabi flow on CP^10 can blow up in finite time even in a class containing a constant scalar curvature metric.
opportunity: None.

title: Affine Bernstein rigidity through dimension nine and a smooth dimension-ten counterexample
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: Complete convex solutions of the affine maximal surface equation are paraboloids in dimensions 3-9, and a smooth non-quadratic entire solution exists in dimension 10.
opportunity: None.
caveats: Dims 3-9 graph case Lean-formalized; dim-10 counterexample not.

title: The isoperimetric profile of the cubic three-torus
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: In a unit cube with periodic boundary conditions, the least-surface-area way to enclose a given volume fraction v (<=1/2) is a sphere for v <= 4*pi/81 (~0.155), a cylinder for v up to 1/pi (~0.318), and a flat slab beyond that -- and nothing else ever wins.
constructive: yes - exact closed-form profile and complete list of minimizers (Theorem intro:main)
explicit_constants: fully explicit: I(V)=min{(36pi)^(1/3) v^(2/3), 2 sqrt(pi v), 2}, transitions 4pi/81 and 1/pi
opportunity: Molecular simulations of liquid-vapour (or any two-phase) coexistence in cubic periodic boxes interpret finite-size effects with the capillarity approximation: the condensed phase is assumed to be a sphere, then a cylinder, then a slab, with crossovers at exactly 4pi/81 and 1/pi (Binder/MacDowell; Prestipino et al., PRE 92, 022141, 2015). Those values came from comparing only the three candidate shapes. The theorem proves that for isotropic sharp-interface energy no other morphology (perforated slabs, Schwarz/gyroid-type periodic surfaces) is ever a global minimizer, so the formulas are exact for the model. That certifies the shape assumption behind slab-geometry interfacial-tension estimates. It also confirms that triply periodic minimal-surface phases in materials (copolymer gyroid, lipid cubic phases) cannot come from interfacial area alone in a cubic cell. Some other energy term is needed.
targets: Finite-size vapour-liquid coexistence analysis in periodic boxes (Binder, MacDowell, Virnau; Prestipino et al. 2015)
Slab/direct-coexistence interfacial-tension workflows in MD/MC codes (GROMACS, LAMMPS, NIST FEASST flat-histogram MC)
Sharp-interface limits of Cahn-Hilliard / Ohta-Kawasaki (block-copolymer) models on cubic periodic cells
first_step: Write a short note or comment for the finite-size coexistence literature saying that the sphere/cylinder/slab sequence and the 4pi/81, 1/pi crossovers are now a theorem for cubic boxes (Lean-formalized). Then list the non-cubic box shapes that slab simulations actually use, as the open extension.
caveats: Applies only to the unit cubic torus. Elongated boxes, which slab simulations usually use, are not covered. Real systems add thermal fluctuations (the transitions are finite-size crossovers), Tolman/curvature corrections and anisotropic tension; copolymers add chain stretching. The transition values were already in the physics literature, and only the 'no other shapes' part is new. This is not the Kelvin/Weaire-Phelan foam-partition problem.
evidence: Web: arXiv 1509.02324 (Prestipino et al., droplet shapes in a periodic box; sph->cyl at 4pi/81, cyl->slab at 1/pi)

title: Unique tangent flows at the first surface singularity
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: When a smooth closed surface moving by mean curvature flow in R^3 first becomes singular, the blow-up limit at each singular point is unique (a single self-shrinker, including its position and axes).
opportunity: None. Mean-curvature smoothing in geometry processing (Desbrun et al., conformalized MCF) and level-set MCF in imaging/grain-growth codes operate on discretizations and viscosity solutions; tangent-flow uniqueness is a step in the theory of flow through singularities, not an algorithmic input.
caveats: Unformalized; major step in MCF singularity theory.

title: Gigli’s characterization of Alexandrov curvature
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: A metric space is an Alexandrov space with curvature >= kappa exactly when it is an RCD((n-1)kappa, n) space with Hausdorff measure whose distributional sectional curvature is >= kappa (Gigli's conjecture).
opportunity: None. The synthetic curvature notions used in ML (Ollivier/Forman graph Ricci curvature for over-squashing, network analysis) are discrete and not RCD; nothing here is computable from data.
caveats: Companion weak-Hessian theorem Lean-formalized; the main characterization is not.

title: Bi-Lipschitz coordinates at every regular RCD point
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: In limits of manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below (noncollapsed RCD spaces), every point whose tangent cones are all Euclidean has a neighbourhood that maps to R^n with distortion at most a constant depending only on the dimension.
constructive: partial - charts built from harmonic coordinates plus a multiscale 'stretching' correction; neighbourhood size uncontrolled and L_n obtained via compactness
explicit_constants: L_n depends only on n but is not computed; chart radius not quantified
opportunity: The closest applied analogue is the theory behind eigenmap/diffusion-map manifold learning: Jones-Maggioni-Schul give local bi-Lipschitz charts from Laplacian eigenfunctions on smooth manifolds. This result extends 'bounded-distortion harmonic-type charts' to singular spaces with Ricci lower bounds, which could in principle support guarantees for data concentrated near singular sets. Without a quantitative chart scale it gives no sample-complexity or algorithmic statement.
targets: Manifold-learning theory (Laplacian eigenmaps / diffusion maps guarantees)
first_step: Find out whether the chart radius can be bounded in terms of volume ratio or Reifenberg flatness. That is the minimum needed before any learning-theory use.
caveats: Not constructive from samples. ML 'curvature' on graphs is not RCD. The constant comes from a compactness argument.

title: A three-manifold without conjugate points or nonpositive curvature
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: There is a closed 3-manifold carrying a metric without conjugate points but no metric of nonpositive curvature.
opportunity: None.

title: Negative Kähler curvature without bounded holomorphic coordinates
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: A contractible domain in C^3 can carry a complete Kahler metric of pinched negative curvature yet not be biholomorphic to any bounded domain.
opportunity: None.
caveats: Pinched example Lean-formalized; one-sided example not.

title: Weak MTW curvature gives convexity and regular optimal transport
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: On any compact Riemannian manifold satisfying the weak Ma-Trudinger-Wang curvature condition, the optimal-transport (squared geodesic distance) map between densities bounded above and below is a homeomorphism that is Holder continuous in both directions, with constants uniform over the density class. Injectivity domains are convex, which settles Villani's conjecture.
constructive: no - regularity theorem; Holder exponent obtained by contradiction and compactness (paper: 'no explicit exponent')
explicit_constants: none: alpha, C depend only on (M,g,lambda,Lambda) but are not computed
opportunity: The only applied use is as a regularity input for convergence or consistency proofs of OT/Monge-Ampere solvers and OT-map estimators on curved domains: OT mesh adaptation on the sphere for atmospheric models (Weller-Browne-Budd-Cullen, McRae-Cotter-Budd), finite-difference OT on the sphere (Hamfeldt-Turnquist), semi-discrete Newton methods (Kitagawa-Merigot-Thibert), and Riemannian flow matching on spheres and tori. The manifolds people actually use there were already covered: round S^n (Loeper), flat tori (Cordero-Erausquin), RP^3=SO(3) (nonfocal case, Loeper-Villani) and products of round spheres (Figalli-Kim-McCann). So the marginal applied gain is close to zero. The one possibly new case is mixed products such as S^2 x T^k.
targets: Convergence analyses of OT/Monge-Ampere solvers on the sphere (Hamfeldt-Turnquist; McRae-Cotter-Budd OT mesh adaptivity)
Riemannian flow matching / OT-map estimation on spheres and tori
Semi-discrete OT Newton solvers (Kitagawa-Merigot-Thibert) extended to manifolds
first_step: Check whether mixed products such as S^2 x T^k (nonnegative cross-curvature, hence weak MTW, by Kim-McCann) were already covered by Figalli-Kim-McCann 2013. If not, they are the only practically relevant manifolds that this result newly covers.
caveats: Covers squared Riemannian distance cost only. It does NOT cover reflector-antenna (c=-log(1-x.y) or -2log|x-y|) or freeform-lens/refractor costs, whose MTW regularity theory (Wang, Loeper 2011, Gutierrez-Huang) is separate and older. Commercial freeform design (least-squares/SQP methods) does not use these regularity theorems. The exponent is non-explicit, and the result gives no algorithm.
evidence: /root/openai-math/preprints/Uniform-Bi-Holder-Transport-from-Weak-MTW-September-25-2026/build/sections/introduction.tex (Theorem thm:main) and conclusion.tex (Remark: no explicit exponent)
Web: arXiv 2108.00088 (reflector antenna OT on sphere uses cost -2log|x-y|)

title: Failure of integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison
subject: Differential geometry
plain_english: On R^n with nonnegative Ricci curvature, the space of harmonic functions of polynomial growth <= k can exceed the Euclidean dimension (Yau's integer-degree comparison fails; 3D examples with fixed-factor excess).
constructive: yes - explicit metrics (Lean version: dimension 16, degree 50000)
opportunity: None.
